subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Bob Gupta <bob.gupta@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria & next steps

Hi Alice / Bob 

Great to chat this morning  thanks for walking through your goals. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the proposed 3-week POC scope and suggested success criteria so we have a clear evaluation plan: 

POC goals (high level):
- Validate integration of Redwood API for chat generation into ACME Support Assistant
- Demonstrate latency and cost targets on representative traffic
- Verify that streaming + tool-calling meets your UX requirements for RAG workflows

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail):
1) Functional integration: support-assistant can call Redwood generate endpoint, receive streamed tokens, and invoke tool-calls for knowledge lookup.
   - Owner: ACME Eng (integration), Redwood Eng for quick blockers.
2) Latency: 95th percentile response time under 800ms for single-turn queries at a 20rps test load.
   - Measurement: Redwood Console per-route tracing + custom load test logs.
3) Cost/throughput: baseline per-token cost measurement with continuous batching enabled.
   - Target: within 25% of model baseline we demo today.
4) Quality: top-1 response accuracy on 100 eval prompts > 85% (ACME-provided test set).

Timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, share keys, and sample data.
- Week 1: integration + streaming + tool-calling demo.
- Week 2: load tests, cost measurements, quality evals.
- Week 3: wrap-up, findings, and next-steps decision.

Owners / next steps:
- ACME: provide sample data, engineering contact, and a test account for the Support Assistant (Bob to confirm).
- Redwood: provide quickstart SDK snippet, example streaming integration, test keys, and a short runbook for tool-calling.
- Schedule kickoff: propose Wed 6/17 10:00am PT  30 minutes.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart.pdf (SDK snippets), poc-eval-metrics.xlsx (evaluation template)

If this looks good, please confirm owners and the kickoff time and I'll send calendar invites + a shared Slack channel.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alice / Bob  quick technical follow-up from our side. Glad to see owners confirmed. A few integration notes and examples to make the kickoff efficient: 

1) Keys & scoping
- We will create a scoped API key for the ACME POC that limits model access and has a 30-day TTL. If you prefer a short-lived token, we can also generate short-lived JWTs via a one-time exchange. Let us know which you prefer.

2) SDK + API routes
- Recommend using the Redwood JS SDK for the initial integration. Example (streaming generation + tool-calling stub):

// pseudocode
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_POC_KEY });
const stream = client.responses.stream({ model: 'redwood-llm-13b', input: userPrompt, tools: ["kb_lookup"] });
stream.on('token', t => sendToFrontend(t));
stream.on('tool_call', call => {
  // call your knowledge endpoint using call.input.docId
});

- If you prefer direct HTTP, the equivalent endpoint is POST /v1/responses with "stream": true.

3) Streaming considerations
- For the UX you described, use streaming for tokens and separate tool-call events. We support delta updates and finalization events. We will provide a small client helper to map tool_call events to outbound HTTP requests.

4) Tool-calling
- Two modes: synchronous HTTP callback (redwood invokes your endpoint) or client-side tool invocation (your client performs lookup). For the POC we recommend client-side invocation to avoid exposing internal endpoints.

5) Load testing & tracing
- Provide a test harness (curl+k6 script) we can run against your staging workload. Redwood Console will capture per-route traces and token counts; we'll share a dashboard link post-kickoff.

6) Next actions before kickoff
- ACME: share sample data + a staging URL for the Support Assistant.
- ACME: confirm key preference (scoped key vs short-lived token).
- Redwood: create scoped key and share SDK quickstart + runbook (we'll attach redwood-quickstart.pdf).

I'll be on the kickoff to walk through the SDK snippet and do a live streaming demo.

Cheers,
Rishi
Staff Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
